name: 80K Hours Upskilling Resources
current_details: A curated list of 67 resources for upskilling in technical AI safety research, compiled by 80,000 Hours with input from their advisors. It covers field overviews (AISafety.com, Anthropic's recommended research agendas, Coefficient Giving, Redwood's control work), technical courses (ARENA, BlueDot Impact, Karpathy's Zero to Hero, Jacob Hilton's Deep Learning Curriculum, Google ML Course), project ideas in evals and mech interp, researcher advice (Neel Nanda, Ethan Perez, Richard Ngo, Marius Hobbhahn), fellowships (Anthropic AI Safety Fellowship, MATS, Constellation Astra, LASR Labs, SPAR, Pivotal, ARENA Cambridge, ERA AI, CHAI, Global AI Safety Fellowship), and profiles of key organisations (AE Studio, ARC, Apollo, CHAI, Conjecture, FAR AI, METR, Palisade, Redwood). Written by Matt Beard, first published June 4, 2025 and last updated September 15, 2025 — a permanent resource page with no application deadline.

name: 80K Hours AI Safety Career Review
current_details: A comprehensive 80,000 Hours career review by Benjamin Hilton (last updated August 2024, first published June 2023) on AI safety technical research, covering two main paths: empirical AI safety — open to strong software engineers who can apply for research contributor roles immediately, even without an ML background — and theoretical AI safety, suited to those with very strong maths or theoretical CS backgrounds, or who could get into a top 10 ML PhD program. It reviews why the work is high impact, the downsides and risk of doing harm, earnings, how to predict personal fit, learning resources, whether to do a PhD, job-hunting strategies, and key organisations (including teams at Google DeepMind, OpenAI, MIT, Cambridge, CMU and UC Berkeley). The review notes the field is highly neglected — an estimated ~300 people worked on technical approaches to AI existential risk as of 2022 — and links to 80,000 Hours' job board, AI career advisor and free 1-on-1 advising.

name: AISafety.com Events & Training

current_details: AISafety.com maintains a continuously updated directory of 120 AI safety training programs — fellowships, bootcamps, courses, and immersive workshops, online and in person — alongside 37 events, 575 jobs, 61 funding sources, 270 communities, 29 self-study resources, a 380-entry field map, media channels, and a founder toolkit. It currently lists 58 upcoming training programs, filterable by type, focus (technical/governance/general), entry bar, stipend, length, and location, with durations from 2 days to 1 year. name: AISafety.com Self-Study
current_details: A curated directory of 29 self-study curricula and reading lists for learning AI safety independently, spanning general introductions (BlueDot's Future of AI and Intro to Transformative AI, Lens Academy's AI Risk Fundamentals based on "If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies", DeepMind's 75-minute AGI Safety Short Course, AI Safety Atlas, CAIS's AISES, ERIC, Intro to Cooperative AI, Reading What We Can), technical alignment training (ARENA, Introduction to ML Safety, Agent Foundations for Superintelligence-Robust Alignment, Iliad Intensive, Harvard CS 2881, Stanford's Introduction to AI Safety, UChicago XLab AI Security Guide and XLab Tracks, Meridian/C2D3's 16-lecture Language Models and Intelligent Agentic Systems, Key Phenomena in AI Risk) and governance/strategy material (ENAIS Deep Dive, AGI Strategy, MATS AI Safety Strategy Curriculum, Economics of Transformative AI, Redwood's AI Futurism Reading List). Each entry is tagged by category (general intro, technical alignment, governance, strategy) and type (curriculum vs. reading list), with no application process or deadline. It is a permanently maintained reference hub run by AISafety.com, alongside their directories of jobs (575), training programs (120), events (37), funding (61) and communities (270).

name: Apart Research Hackathons
current_deadline: Next Sprint: Threat Intelligence & Threat Modelling Hackathon, Dec 4–6, 2026
current_details: Apart Research runs weekend research sprints (hackathons) on a single AI safety question, open to anyone worldwide, held online and at local in-person sites. Standout participants are invited to Apart Studio, the route into the Apart Fellowship, while Partnered Fellowships accept direct applications. The organization focuses on manipulation and dark patterns in frontier AI systems, with work published at NeurIPS 2025 (sandbagging/noise injection) and ICLR 2025 (DarkBench, oral).

name: BlueDot Impact
current_deadline: Nov 22, 2026 (Technical AI Safety & Biosecurity); AGI Strategy Nov 29; Frontier AI Governance Dec 6, 2026 — grants rolling
current_details: BlueDot Impact is a philanthropic startup building the AI safety and biosecurity workforce through free cohort-based online courses, in-person programs, and grants, having trained 10,000+ professionals since 2022 and granted $11.4M. Courses (AGI Strategy, Technical AI Safety, Frontier AI Governance, Biosecurity) run 25–40 hours each, either in one intensive week or part-time, with small facilitated discussion groups; a free 90-minute intro course needs no application. In-person offerings include Incubator Week in San Francisco (up to $200k backing) and an AI Security Bootcamp, plus rolling Rapid (up to $20k), Career Transition, Media, and Seed Grants of $20k–$200k.

name: Google DeepMind: AGI Safety Short Course
current_details: A free, self-paced introductory course on AGI safety from Google DeepMind's safety research team, comprising ~75 minutes of short recorded talks and exercises plus a slide deck and exercise workbook. It covers the path to superhuman capabilities, risks from deliberate planning and instrumental subgoals, how misaligned goals arise (specification gaming vs. goal misgeneralization), DeepMind's technical alignment approach (amplified oversight, robust training & monitoring, security & control, interpretability, safer design patterns, alignment stress tests), and its governance approach including frontier safety practices and dangerous capability evaluations. Aimed at students, researchers and professionals who want an accessible one-hour introduction to AI alignment.

name: MATS Slack #opportunities
current_details: Contract work, facilitation gigs, paper reviews, and collaboration opportunities from the MATS community.

name: Outsider's Roadmap to AI Safety (LessWrong)
current_details: A comprehensive guide published in July 2025 for professionals transitioning into AI safety research from technical backgrounds such as software engineering, physics, or data science. Covers three critical domains: interpretability research (reverse-engineering AI systems to understand their inner workings), alignment research (ensuring AI systems remain beneficial and share human values), and AI control & governance (technical policy for advanced systems). Written by someone actively making the transition, synthesizing insights from Neel Nanda's mechanistic interpretability resources, 80,000 Hours career research, and the broader alignment community, with practical advice on evolving roles (the shift from separate research engineers/scientists toward 'full-stack researchers'), required skills, and pathways for newcomers to contribute meaningfully to the field.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
current_deadline: Rolling (January 2027 cohort deadline of October 18, 2026 has passed)
current_details: The Anthropic Fellows Program funds and mentors engineers and researchers tackling Anthropic's highest-priority AI safety questions — scalable oversight, adversarial robustness and AI control, model organisms, mechanistic interpretability, AI security, and model welfare. Fellows spend 4 months on empirical research with an Anthropic mentor, receiving ~$15K/month in compute funding plus a stipend (see the job description for current rates). No PhD, prior ML experience, or published papers required; more than 200 fellows have participated since early 2025, with over 65% publishing their work and over 35% joining Anthropic full-time.

name: CAIS AI & Society Fellowship
current_details: A fully-funded, three-month in-person fellowship at CAIS in San Francisco for scholars in economics, law, international relations, and adjacent disciplines to pursue self-directed research on AI's societal impacts. Fellows receive a $25,000 stipend plus covered travel and daily lunch and dinner, and take part in guest speaker events, workshops, and a closing workshop where they present interim research outputs. Open to professors, PhD/JD holders or students, and researchers with equivalent experience; no prior AI research required, and participation is in-person by default.

name: CBAI Summer Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Rolling — Expression of Interest open for Spring 2026
current_details: The Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative (CBAI) Research Fellowship is an intensive, fully-funded ten-week program in Cambridge, Massachusetts for researchers building careers in technical AI safety, AI governance, or technical governance. Fellows receive an $8,000 stipend, housing for non-local participants, weekday meals, 24/7 Harvard Square workspace, up to $10,000 in compute credits, and 1–2 hours weekly of mentorship from researchers at Harvard, MIT, Google DeepMind, the UK AI Security Institute, CNAS, RAND, and the Institute for Progress. Open to undergraduates, master's and PhD students, postdocs, and early-career professionals (18+; OPT/CPT accepted but no visa sponsorship), with an extension program of up to 4 months available.

name: ERA Fellowship (Cambridge)
current_deadline: Closed — Winter 2027 cycle runs Jan 18 – Mar 26, 2027
current_details: The ERA:AI Fellowship is a 10-week intensive research programme in Cambridge, UK across three tracks: technical AI safety, AI governance, and technical AI governance. Fellows receive a competitive stipend, meals during working hours, covered transport and visas, dedicated research management support, and a generous compute budget, plus mentorship from experts across government, academia and industry (University of Cambridge, UK AI Security Institute, GovAI, RAND, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic). The cohort experience includes 30+ events and a community of 200+ alumni now at organisations like the UK AI Security Institute, European AI Office, CAISI, METR, Apollo Research and Anthropic.

current_deadline: Closed — final deadline was 31 December 2024; expressions of interest accepted for the second iteration
current_details: Impact Academy's Global AI Safety Fellowship is a fully funded research program placing exceptional STEM talent with leading AI safety organisations including CHAI (UC Berkeley), Conjecture, FAR.AI, and the UK AI Safety Institute. Fellows work full-time for up to 6 months (or longer) and receive up to $30,000, plus an optional fully-funded AI safety bootcamp, mentorship, 1:1 coaching, and visa/logistics support. A cohort of 10–20 fellows is selected worldwide via a two-phase, 4–6 week process requiring demonstrated ML/deep learning knowledge, programming experience, and scholastic excellence.

name: Iliad Intensive / Fellowship
current_details: Iliad advances AI alignment as a theoretical and experimental science through in-house research, incubated organizations (AIXI Labs, Principia, Stormglass, XOR Labs), the peer-reviewed Alignment Journal, and training programs. The Iliad Intensive is a 4-week taught program in foundational alignment for technically strong researchers, and the Iliad Fellowship is a ~3-month mentored research program in London or the Bay Area for scholars pivoting into mathematical and theoretical AI safety (Fellows must have completed the Intensive). Research areas include learning theory, debate, heuristic arguments, data attribution, agency, and the geometry of neural networks; about half of Fellows receive a six-month research extension.

name: MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars)
current_deadline: Closed - check for next cycle (mentor applications open for Summer & Autumn 2027)
current_details: MATS is an independent research fellowship that connects talented researchers with top mentors in machine alignment, transparency, and security. Fellows conduct research for 12 weeks at offices in Berkeley, CA and London, UK, with the opportunity to apply for an additional 6–12 month funded extension. MATS also runs a Residency for long-horizon AI safety research, and mentor applications are currently open for the Summer and Autumn 2027 cohorts.

name: AE Studio — AI Alignment Research Grants
current_details: The AI Alignment Foundation (the alignment arm spun out of AE Studio) provides research funding plus dedicated engineering teams to pursue high-risk, high-reward alignment directions beyond mechanistic interpretability, evals, and control. It targets alignment researchers with ideas their institutional funding won't cover, plus technical experts from other fields (cognitive neuroscience, mathematics, physics) whose perspectives could open new directions. Engineering teams can execute proposals with as little as one hour per week of the researcher's time, and applicants are asked to describe a first experiment a good engineering team could run in 1–2 weeks.

structured.location: Marina Del Rey, CA (remote applicants welcome)

name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
current_details: A 15-week full-time, in-person AI safety research fellowship in London (18 January – 30 April 2027) based at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA), with weekly 1-on-1 mentorship from established researchers, dedicated research managers, workshops and speaker sessions. Fellows receive a £15,000–£18,000 stipend, travel to London, £1,800/month housing support for non-London fellows, weekday lunch and dinner, and compute. Open to anyone 18 or older regardless of academic background; selection involves a written application, short video interview, mentor-specific work task, and a final interview.

name: Second Look Research (UChicago XLab)
current_details: Second Look Research is a project of the Existential Risk Lab (XLab) at the University of Chicago that produces open-source replications of load-bearing empirical results in AI safety. Its Second Look Fellows program is a 10-week, in-person research program at the University of Chicago where each fellow owns replication projects from scoping through implementation and write-up. The site also publishes completed replications (most recently November 2026) and hosts forms for feedback or to request a specific replication.

name: SPAR
current_deadline: Spring 2027 applications open December 16, 2026 and close January 13, 2027 (mentor/org applications close November 30, 2026)
current_details: SPAR (run by Kairos) is a 3-month, flexible remote fellowship pairing aspiring AI safety, policy, biosecurity, communications and fieldbuilding contributors with experienced mentors from Anthropic, Google DeepMind, UK AISI, Stanford, FAR.AI and more. Fellows commit 5–40 hours/week alongside other work, produce output that has reached ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS and TIME coverage, and present at a virtual Demo Day with $7,000 in prizes plus a career fair with METR, Redwood Research and GovAI. Open to any experience level, from undergraduates to experienced professionals; an expression-of-interest form is open ahead of the Spring 2027 round, which newly includes non-research projects.

name: Coefficient Giving — Transition Grants

current_details: Coefficient Giving's Career Development and Transition Funding provided grants to individuals at any career stage building career capital for work reducing global catastrophic risks, with particular interest in AI safety and global catastrophic biological risks. It funded graduate study, unpaid internships, independent study, career transition and exploration periods, postdocs, professional certifications, online courses, and sabbaticals, was open to applicants in any country, and had no minimum or maximum number of grants. The program was handed over to BlueDot Impact on September 4, 2026 — prospective applicants should apply through BlueDot's career transition and rapid grants programs, while existing grantees can still contact careerdevelopmentfunding@coefficientgiving.org.

name: Coefficient Giving — Technical AI Safety RFP
current_details: Coefficient Giving's (formerly Open Philanthropy) request for proposals for technical AI safety research covering 21 research areas across five clusters: adversarial machine learning, sophisticated misbehavior in LLMs, model transparency, trust from first principles, and alternative approaches to mitigating AI risks. The fund expected to deploy roughly $40M over 5 months, with grants ranging from rapid API-credit funding to seed funding for new research organizations. Applications were submitted via an expression of interest (EOI) form, with a 3-month grace period for revise-and-resubmit and late applicants.

name: Foresight Institute AI Nodes
current_details: Foresight Institute's AI for Science & Safety Nodes RFP offers grant funding, office space, and access to private local compute clusters at physical hubs in San Francisco and Berlin, plus a community xNode in Cape Town with the Cape Institute for Safe AI (CISAI). The call spans three areas: I. Local Compute, II. Coordination and accountability, and III. AI-first science (Bio, Neuro, Nano), with grants typically $30,000–$100,000 (larger amounts possible for the right project). Individuals, teams, non-profits and for-profits may apply; strong priority goes to applicants who will be active, in-person contributors at the Nodes, and review takes roughly three months after the deadline. Foresight also accepts ongoing expressions of interest from teams wanting to launch their own independent AI Node, and is recruiting technical grant advisors.

structured.location: San Francisco & Berlin (xNode in Cape Town)

A legacy LTFF page remains online but no longer accepts applications or donations — applicants and donors are directed to the Transformative AI Fund instead.

name: Manifund Regranting
current_details: Manifund's AI Safety Regranting program gives expert regrantors independent budgets of $100K–$350K to fund AI safety projects sourced from their own networks or from Manifund's open call. Because a single regrantor owns each budget rather than a committee, grants can be approved in days rather than months, with example regrants ranging from $11K to $200K. Manifund's 501c3 fiscal sponsorship lets regrantors fund individuals, unregistered projects, and (pending diligence) for-profits, and every grant — including the regrantor's written rationale — is published publicly.

name: Meridian Cambridge — Research Accelerator Week
current_details: An intensive 6-day programme in Cambridge, UK (18–23 May 2026) that moves technical AI safety researchers into funded independent research via a dedicated Coefficient Giving funding pathway. Participants meet 30+ researchers to form teams, submit an EOI on Day 3 (24-hour response), and leave with a completed grant proposal, plus fiscal sponsorship through Meridian and automatic consideration for a 3-12 month Visiting Researcher Programme residency in central Cambridge. Workspace, accommodation, meals, visa support and travel reimbursement (up to £200 UK, £400 Europe, £700 international) are covered; the previous cohort secured over $1M in funding, with funding decisions typically within 8-12 weeks.

Two tiers were offered — Tier 1 up to $300,000 and Tier 2 $300,000–$1,000,000 — for 1–2 year projects across four research clusters: sandboxes and testbeds, the science of agent networks, strengthening agent infrastructure, and multi-agent oversight and control. The call opened June 11, 2026, held informational webinars on June 30 and July 23, and funding decisions are expected in Autumn 2026.

current_details: The Alignment Project is a global AI alignment research fund launched in 2025 by an international coalition including the UK AI Security Institute, CAISI, CIFAR, Australia's AI Safety Institute, OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, Anthropic, Schmidt Sciences, Halcyon Futures, Renaissance Philanthropy, UKRI and ARIA. It awards grants of £50,000 to £1,000,000 to researchers across disciplines — from computer science to cognitive science — plus dedicated cloud compute and API credits, potential venture investment, and hands-on support from AISI's Alignment team. Round 1 awarded over £27 million across more than 60 projects, spanning priority areas such as interpretability, learning theory, cryptography, cognitive science and AI monitoring.

name: 5050 AI (Fifty Years)
current_details: 5050 AI is a 13-week, entirely free accelerator from Fifty Years that helps AI researchers turn their research into deep tech startups focused on AI safety and alignment — no equity, no fees, no weird clauses. Sessions run in SF, Boston and remotely, plus a UK track in London in partnership with ARIA, with the cohort flown in for kickoff and a 3-day off-the-grid camp weekend; mentors include Wojciech Zaremba, Emmett Shear, Ross Girshick, Dileep George, and Ronnie Chatterji. 340 scientists and engineers have gone through the program, launching 78 companies with a 95% seed raise success rate.

name: Catalyze Impact
current_details: Catalyze Impact is a 501(c)(3) non-profit incubator that helps exceptional founders launch AI safety, security, and resilience organizations — helping them choose the right problem, then connecting them with funders and domain experts. Since 2023 it has helped launch 20+ organizations that have collectively raised more than $190M. It also runs two seed/pre-seed Funding Networks (an investor network and a grantmaker Seed Funding Circle, each for those deploying $50K+ per year), with rounds 2–4 times a year where $50K–$300K can launch a new organization.

name: Halcyon Futures
current_details: Halcyon Futures is a grant-maker, incubator and investment firm backing exceptional founders building in AI safety, cybersecurity and biosecurity. It combines grants, incubation support and venture investment to build organizations focused on resilience for the era of transformative AI, with a portfolio of launched ventures and supported career transitions. Prospective founders can reach the team directly at hello@halcyonfutures.org.

name: ImpactOps
current_details: Impact Ops is an operations consultancy providing hands-on specialist support to high-impact organizations across AI safety, global health and development, animal welfare, and climate change. Services span six areas — finance (budgets to bookkeeping), recruitment, entity setup and fiscal-sponsor spin-outs, donor/grantee due diligence, operational audits, and systems implementation. Clients include the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, BlueDot Impact, Foresight Institute, Forecasting Research Institute, Longview Philanthropy, Giving What We Can, Condor Initiative, Food Policy Pathways, and The Earthshot Prize, with a Careers page and contact form for engaging services.

name: Rethink Priorities Special Projects
current_details: Rethink Priorities' Special Projects Program provides fiscal sponsorship and end-to-end operational support — tax-exempt grant receipt, finance and accounting, recruitment and hiring via US/UK entities or an international Employer of Record, visa facilitation, fundraising coordination, and event planning — so high-impact initiatives can launch and scale fast. Fees for new projects are typically around 14% of project costs, varying with needs, complexity, and scale. Figures through the end of 2025: 195 expressions of interest received, 15 projects supported, $19.7M in direct costs expended, 114 sponsee staff onboarded, 16 completed hiring rounds (three ongoing), 32 successful US/UK visa applications, and 20 in-person events with 500 attendees.

name: Seldon Lab
current_details: Seldon Lab is an accelerator and venture studio that invests in and builds alongside founders working exclusively on world-scale AGI deployment and existential security technologies. Beyond capital and mentorship, the team publishes papers, builds systems, and deploys cyber-physical infrastructure, with event guests including Geoff Ralston, Emmett Shear, and Josh Achiam and a team including Eric Ries, Esben Kran, Finn Metz, and Nick Fitz. Portfolio founders include Lucid Computing and Andon Labs from Batch #1; Batch #2's Demo Day took place Apr 20, 2026, and applications are accepted on a rolling basis via the site's Apply Now page.

name: WorkStream
current_details: WorkStream Nonprofit (High Impact Alliance, a 501(c)(3), EIN 99-3881534) provides operations consulting and embedded implementation support for small and mid-sized nonprofits, including workflow optimization, fractional COO leadership, technology implementation, executive support, and hiring/recruitment. Its flagship six-month Operations Accelerator pairs workshops, coaching, and peer accountability for organizations of 4-20 staff, alongside the GRIP growth-readiness assessment (10 indicators), fiscal sponsorship and advisory pathways, and courses. The team, guided by effective altruism principles, has supported groups such as the Center for AI Safety and Rooted Futures Lab, with engagements and conversations started on a rolling basis.

name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
current_details: The 80,000 Hours Job Board is a continuously updated, handpicked listing of high-impact roles tackling pressing global problems, with a strong emphasis on AI safety, AI policy, and existential risk reduction. Users can search and filter by annualised, USD-converted salary, location and role type, exclude career-development roles, save or hide listings, see personalised matches based on their background, and subscribe to daily or weekly job alerts. It sits alongside free 1-1 career advice, an AI advisor chat, and 80,000 Hours' research including the career guide, AI careers, top skills and list of world problems.

name: AISafety.com Jobs
current_details: AISafety.com Jobs is a continuously updated job board now listing 575 open roles (plus 5 more) spanning AI safety research, policy, software engineering, operations, communications and security. Recent listings include MIT FutureTech, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, FAR AI, Encode, the AI Alignment Foundation, Constellation, Pour Demain, Global Shield and the National Research Council Canada, with advertised pay from around $90,000 to $450,000 (plus UK roles up to £640,000, CAD 119,688–168,192, CHF 105,000–125,000 and €65,000–€80,000). Roles range from entry-level to chief-officer leadership, many remote or based in the San Francisco Bay Area, London, Washington DC, Ottawa and across Europe, and many don't require technical skills.

name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
current_details: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is a San Francisco-based AI safety non-profit working to reduce societal-scale risks from AI through research, field-building, and advocacy. Its careers page currently lists no specific open roles, but invites interested candidates to email hiring@safe.ai with questions, and researchers can submit a collaboration form to work with CAIS.

name: FAR AI Careers
current_details: FAR AI's careers landing page is a high-level invitation to join a team working toward trustworthy and secure AI, organized around three pillars: a portfolio of research agendas, events convening global AI leaders, and field-building programs. The page lists no individual roles, deadlines, salaries, or locations — specific openings live elsewhere on the site and are generally filled on a rolling basis.

name: MATS Alumni Hiring Database
current_details: A signup form to create an account for the MATS Alumni Hiring Database, which connects alumni of the MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) Program with organizations hiring in AI safety. Registration requires only a full name, email, and agreement to the MATS Privacy Policy. This resource is exclusively for MATS program alumni.

name: MATS Careers (Staff Hiring)
current_details: MATS is the Berkeley-based AI safety research mentorship program, and its careers page covers staff hiring to support its fellowship and research operations. The page currently lists no specific open staff roles — instead it directs prospective applicants to submit a general Expression of Interest form, which is reviewed as new positions open. MATS looks for people motivated by AI alignment, transparency, and security, with the skills to support cutting-edge research operations.

structured.location: Berkeley, CA (with some London-based roles historically)

name: What AI Safety Orgs Want in a Hire
current_details: Blog post from 80,000 Hours (published September 23, 2025) by Conor Barnes summarising a survey of 38 leaders of top AI safety organisations about their hiring needs. Key findings: 1–3 years of relevant experience is often enough for non-technical-research and policy roles, and the most-recommended upskilling routes are BlueDot courses, the Talos Fellowship, MATS, GovAI fellowships, the Cambridge ERA:AI Fellowship, and Pivotal Research. It stresses publishing work publicly and networking at events like EA Global, notes the hardest-to-fill profiles (chiefs of staff, policy experience, Mandarin speakers, European citizens with AI context), and links to the 80,000 Hours job board with 300+ AI safety roles.

name: Apollo Research
current_details: Apollo Research hires across technical research, engineering, governance, and operations for its AI security work on frontier model scheming, deception, AI control, and loss-of-control risks, including its Watcher product. Most staff are based in London or San Francisco with regular in-office collaboration and flexible hours; benefits include competitive salary and equity, pension/401(k) matching, unlimited PTO, private medical insurance, 6 months paid parental leave, an annual professional development budget, and visa sponsorship plus relocation support. Hiring runs through an application screen, a 30-minute screening call, a 2-2.5 hour take-home, three 60-minute role-specific interviews, and a final leadership interview, with candidates typically starting within 3 months; no internships are offered and rejected applicants may re-apply after 6 months.

name: Beneficial AI Foundation
current_details: The Beneficial AI Foundation (founded by Max Tegmark) is hiring for fully remote roles focused on researching how to keep AI beneficial for generations to come. Open positions include AI Safety Research Scientist (starting at $35–$75/hour, depending on experience and qualifications) and Research Engineer (starting at $30–$70/hour, commensurate with track record and demonstrated potential). Both roles are remote from anywhere with no stated application deadline.

name: Forethought
current_details: Forethought Research is a non-profit studying how to navigate rapid AI progress and the transition to superintelligent AI, with work spanning AI-driven progress modeling, AI-enabled coups, governance, deep space resource governance, and long-run strategy. Three openings are listed with no application deadline: a general researcher expression of interest, one focused on extreme power concentration, and a Founders Fellowship. Roles are based in Oxford or Berkeley (remote negotiable, UK visa sponsorship usually available), with 33 days annual leave, a £5k/yr professional development budget, 14 weeks full-pay parental leave, and a pension with 2x employer match up to £10k/yr.

name: Goodfire
current_details: Goodfire is an AI interpretability startup hiring agentic, mission-driven people to advance understanding of AI systems, with product lines spanning LLMs and life sciences. All roles are full-time, in person five days a week at their San Francisco (Telegraph Hill) office. Open roles are listed on the careers page, with a full listing hosted on Greenhouse.

name: Gray Swan AI
current_details: Gray Swan AI is an AI security company building adversarial evaluation and red-teaming tools (Shade, Cygnal, and the Arena red-teaming network), with research that has directly informed the safety evaluations of frontier models including Claude, GPT, and Gemini. The careers page currently highlights Software Engineer openings, reviewed on a rolling basis. Benefits include 28 days off between holidays and PTO, 401(k) with up to 4% matching, flexible work arrangements, visa sponsorship, professional development support, medical/dental/vision coverage, catered lunches at the Pittsburgh office, and 100% paid parental leave with up to 14 weeks of paid birthing leave.

name: LawZero
current_details: LawZero is a non-profit AI safety lab founded by Yoshua Bengio, based in Montreal with many roles also open in Berlin, building safe-by-design, non-agentic AI to accelerate scientific discovery and provide oversight of agentic AI systems. Its Greenhouse board currently lists roughly 16 postings across research, engineering, legal and operations, including Director of Evaluations, Machine Learning Manager, Mathematical Scientist for AI Safety Research, Senior ML Research Scientist, Senior Researcher, Senior ML Research Developer, Senior ML Data Processing Developer, Senior Distributed ML Engineer, Senior Data Platform Engineer, Senior Counsel (Corporate Governance), Senior Manager of Government Partnerships, Accounting Technician, Communications Specialist and Technical Recruiter. An expression-of-interest form for 2027 internships and a Talent Community sign-up for future opportunities are also available.

name: METR (formerly ARC Evals)
current_details: METR (formerly ARC Evals) is a research nonprofit conducting empirical research to measure AI capabilities, autonomy, and catastrophic risk, with work underpinning evaluation standards (STREAM, AEF-1) and frontier safety policies. Current openings are Member of Policy Staff, Government Affairs (Washington, D.C., on-site, $306K–$471K), Head of Development (Berkeley, $206K–$306K), and Head of People (Berkeley, $223K–$260K), plus a flexible-location General Expression of Interest. Benefits include a 401k with 100% match up to 8%, medical/dental/vision, fertility support via Carrot with 21-week parental leave, unlimited PTO, relocation support, and wellness, commuter, professional development, and management coaching budgets.

name: MIRI TGT Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - register interest for future cohorts
current_details: MIRI's Technical Governance Team runs a small research fellowship where fellows pick a scoped project from the team's list (or design their own) at the intersection of technical and political AI governance — adversarial detection of ML training on monitored GPUs, chip production monitoring during a capabilities halt, confidence-building measures for international agreements, interconnect bandwidth limits, and U.S. executive legal powers over AI. The program runs 8 weeks at 40 hours/week with a $1,200/week stipend ($9,600 total), remote-by-default with an in-person kickoff week in Berkeley, CA (flights and housing provided). A main goal is identifying full-time hires; strong applicants care deeply about existential risk and have research or policy experience, and visas cannot be sponsored.

structured.location: Remote-by-default, kickoff week in Berkeley, CA
structured.program_dates: An 8-week period between Feb 2, 2026 and Aug 31, 2026

name: Redwood Research
current_details: Redwood Research is hiring in Berkeley, California (on-site) for technical roles — Empirical Researcher and Conceptual Reasoning Capabilities Researcher, both paying $350K–$850K — plus generalist roles including a People Operations Lead ($200K–$250K) and IT Systems Administrator ($250K–$300K). A general expression of interest option is also open, and candidates are expected to have a deep interest in AI safety, strong communication skills, and (for technical roles) machine learning and software engineering experience. The page also points to the MATS program and Constellation Astra Fellowship for fellowship-style opportunities.

name: SAIF (Safe AI Forum)
current_details: SAIF (Safe AI Forum) fosters international collaboration on AI safety, convening researchers and policymakers through initiatives such as IDAIS. The organisation currently has no open roles, but it continues to welcome expressions of interest via its contact form from talented individuals passionate about its mission, including those whose skillsets don't match a current opening.

name: Simplex
current_details: Simplex is an AI safety research organization founded in 2024 by Paul Riechers and Adam Shai, building a science of intelligence through computational mechanics and interpretability — covering belief state geometry, constrained belief updating, in-context learning, quantum/post-quantum representations, and factored world models in transformers. They are currently hiring Research Scientists in the Bay Area and Research Scientists in London. Recent output includes a 2026 preprint on reusable composable abstractions in LLMs, a NeurIPS 2026 paper on in-context belief state geometry, and an ICML 2026 paper showing transformers learn factored representations.

name: Transluce
current_details: Transluce is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit research lab building the public tech stack for scalable oversight of AI, including the Docent platform for analyzing AI agent behavior, incident investigations, and independent evaluations. It also founded and chairs the AI Evaluator Forum, a network of third-party evaluators setting standards for meaningful oversight. Hiring runs through a separate 'Careers' page; the main site lists no specific roles, compensation, or application deadlines.

name: WhiteBox Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Cohort 2 ended May 18, 2025 — expression of interest open for future cohorts
current_details: WhiteBox Research runs a 15-week AI Interpretability Fellowship for aspiring researchers in or near Southeast Asia, with an in-person track at Openspace Katipunan in Quezon City, Philippines and a virtual track open to residents of South, Southeast, or East Asia. Fellows learn to train and interpret models like GPT-2 using ARENA-derived exercises and gain research experience through two AI safety hackathons. The program is free (normally $3,000 USD), pays a $200 USD completion reward, and requires at least 15 hours/week.

structured.stipend: $200 USD completion reward (program free, normally $3,000 USD)

name: 80K Hours: Top US Policy Masters Programs
current_details: A curated 80,000 Hours Airtable directory of 12 top US policy master's programs in national security, international affairs, and public policy, nearly all based in Washington, DC. Listings include Georgetown's Security Studies Program, MPP and MS in Biohazardous Threat Agents, RAND School's 9-month Master of National Security Policy and Master of Technology Policy, Johns Hopkins SAIS MAIR, George Mason's MS Biodefense, GWU Security Policy Studies (18 months full-time or up to 5 years part-time), American University's USFP and MPA, Maryland's MPP, and Texas A&M Bush School's 30-credit Master of International Policy. Each record details tuition, duration (9 months to 2 years), full- vs part-time and evening options, class times, GRE/GPA expectations, concentrations, start dates and individual application deadlines.

structured.location: Washington, DC (plus RAND in Santa Monica, CA)

name: aisafety.com/funding
current_details: A continuously maintained directory of 61 AI safety funders — grant programs, pooled funds, regranting platforms, prizes, and philanthropic advisors — covering technical research, governance, field-building, journalism, and career transitions. Listings span micro-grants ($10K BlueDot Rapid Grants up to $20K, Leo Gao's paused Experimental Microgranting, IFP's Launch Sequence honorarium) through mid-scale funds (Transformative AI Fund at $10K–$150K, Mercor's $5M AI Safety Fund, FAR.AI's $12M invite-only grantmaking) to large-scale philanthropy (Coefficient Giving's Project Tailwind at $200K–$200M, the ISPA Inspection Prize at $5M–$20M). Many entries take applications on a rolling basis, a sizeable share are currently closed or invite-only, and a few have fixed windows — Tarbell Institutional Grants ($50K–$500K+) closing 11 Dec 2026 and Lightcone Commons closing 1 Jan 2027.

name: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
current_details: The Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship supports PhD students and early-career researchers working on cooperative AI, multi-agent coordination, and related AI safety problems. The 2026 cohort of 14 fellows was selected from 240 applications (a 35% increase over the inaugural 2025 cohort), with fellows receiving annual budgets for conferences, compute, wellbeing, and productivity, travel funding for CAIF events, and collaboration access with CAIF researchers and partner organisations. CAIF Scholars, ranked in the top 1% of applicants, additionally receive top-up funding of up to $40,000 per year for living expenses for up to 3 years.

structured.stipend: Up to $40,000/year top-up for CAIF Scholars; annual conference, compute, wellbeing and productivity budgets for all fellows
structured.location: Remote / international (fellows at Oxford, Harvard, MIT, CMU and others)

name: Cooperative AI Research Fellowship (Cape Town)
current_details: A full-time 3-month research fellowship in Cape Town, South Africa for researchers from diverse backgrounds to pursue AI safety research from a cooperative AI perspective, spanning multi-agent safety, AI for facilitating human cooperation, mitigating gradual disempowerment, and wildcard projects. Fellows receive a $3,000/month (R53,000) stipend, a private room in a group house, flights to and from Cape Town, office space with workday meals, and a compute budget, plus mentorship from researchers at Google DeepMind, Oxford, and MIT. The 2026 cohort (31 January – 30 April 2026) of 10 fellows has concluded and its research posters are now published.

name: FLI AI Safety PhD Advisor Directory
current_details: A directory of AI researchers and faculty committed to AI existential safety, listing roughly 65 faculty at institutions including Oxford, Cambridge, UC Berkeley, Stanford, MIT, Princeton and CMU, plus 125+ additional AI researchers (12 displayed with 113 more via 'Load more') open to collaborating with and advising students. It is designed as a resource for finding a faculty mentor when applying for FLI's Vitalik Buterin postdoctoral and PhD fellowships, with awarded fellows receiving automatic community membership. Professors and researchers can separately apply for community membership on a rolling basis to access funding for grad students/postdocs, travel support, workshops and networking events.

name: Schmidt Sciences AI2050
current_details: AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative of Schmidt Sciences, conceived and co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, supporting exceptional researchers worldwide working on the hard problems and key opportunities critical to ensuring AI benefits society by 2050. Fellows are named as Early Career or Senior Fellows through a nomination-only process and join an interdisciplinary global research community spanning disciplines and career stages. In November 2025 Schmidt Sciences announced $18M in new awards, following a $10M commitment to AI safety research in February 2025.

name: Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship (FLI)
current_deadline: Closed - check for next cycle (last deadline November 21, 2025; no applications in fall 2026)
current_details: The Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship in AI Existential Safety, run by FLI with the Beneficial AI Foundation, supports incoming and current PhD students working on AI existential safety research. Fellows receive tuition and fees for 5 years (extension possible), a $40,000 annual stipend at US, UK and Canadian universities, a $10,000 research fund for travel and computing, and invitations to field events; short-listed applicants are reimbursed for up to 5 PhD program application fees. FLI has paused the program and will not accept applications in fall 2026 while reassessing its direction, with no timeline announced; awardees must agree to donate half their compensation if they join a frontier AGI lab within 2 years.

name: AI Policy Leadership Network (APLN)
current_details: APLN is a part-time program organized by the Foundation for American Innovation, the Center for a New American Security, and the Horizon Institute for Public Service that convenes experienced AI policy professionals — at least 6 (and up to 25) years of professional experience including 4+ years in AI policy-relevant organizations across government, think tanks, military/intelligence, and industry. The 2026 cohort runs mid-March through late July 2026, with monthly off-the-record evening discussions in Washington, DC and one multi-day learning trip to the San Francisco Bay Area in April 2026. All program expenses including trip travel and accommodations are covered, but no stipend is provided and there is no homework, instruction, or job placement.

structured.location: Washington, DC (plus SF Bay Area trip)

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
current_details: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a bipartisan AI policy nonprofit headquartered at 750 17th St NW in Washington, DC, advocating for a proactive framework for AI policy that safeguards Americans while preserving U.S. competitiveness. Its careers page lists open roles as they become available, and currently no specific positions are posted. ARI also offers a non-employee referral bonus of $3,000 for Director/VP-level hires and $1,500 for all other roles, paid within 60 days after the referred hire completes 30 days of employment.

name: Career Accelerator (Horizon)
current_details: Horizon's Career Accelerator is a 9-month, part-time, remote program to launch a career in AI and technology policy, offering a modular mix of mentorship, guided training modules, application coaching, networking, exclusive opportunity listings, and a peer Slack community, with a time commitment of at most 5 hours per week during the optional training period. Participants can apply for up to $100,000 in flexible funding for unpaid internships, upskilling, conferences, and career transitions. It welcomes students and recent graduates as well as mid-career and senior professionals pivoting into technology policy; international applicants without US work authorization should check the FAQ for eligibility.

name: CNAS Nye Internship
current_deadline: Rolling — target start dates March 2027 and April 2027
current_details: The Joseph S. Nye, Jr. National Security Internship and Mentoring Program places interns directly with a CNAS research program or business department — Communications, Defense, Energy/Economics and Security, Technology and National Security, or Transatlantic Security — for policy research, writing, event support, and exposure to national security policy debates. Internships are full-time (40 hrs/week) for a six-month term in Washington, DC, with a $1,900/month living stipend plus a $75/month transportation stipend. Interns in several programs are expected to produce a written product under their own byline; CNAS asks that application materials not be generated or revised with AI tools.

structured.program_dates: Target start dates: March 2027 (Defense, Transatlantic Security), April 2027 (Energy, Economics and Security; Technology and National Security)

name: CSET Summer Internship (Georgetown)
current_details: A 10-week summer internship at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), where interns work alongside senior researchers on emerging technology and national security topics including AI, cybersecurity, the AI workforce, and biotechnology. The program is designed specifically for students from Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and other Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs), and is cost-free to interns: a competitive hourly wage plus living stipends, paid housing at Georgetown's intern housing (55 H St NW, downtown DC), and travel covered. Interns receive one-on-one mentorship and workshops, and finish by publishing a CSET blog post and presenting their findings; no academic credit is offered.

structured.stipend: Competitive hourly wage + living stipends; housing and travel paid
structured.location: Washington, DC (Georgetown Capitol Campus, 500 1st St NW, Suite 700)

name: GovAI Summer Fellowship
current_details: GovAI's Summer Fellowship is a three-month program running 7 June – 27 August 2027, offered in London on either a Research or Applied track, plus a parallel DC Summer Fellowship in Washington, DC. Fellows pursue an ambitious AI governance project (or, on the Applied Track, a non-research project pitched by GovAI or partners such as the UK AI Security Institute, Longview Philanthropy and Far.AI) with expert guidance, seminars and Q&As. Applications are welcome from anywhere in the world, from early-career candidates to experienced professionals moving into AI governance.

structured.location: London, UK (and Washington, DC for the DC Fellowship)

name: Horizon Fellowship
current_details: The Horizon Fellowship places fully-funded fellows in Washington, DC host organizations — executive branch agencies, congressional offices, national laboratories, and think tanks — to work on AI, biotechnology, and other emerging technology policy. Fellows and senior fellows serve 1-year terms renewable for a second year, while junior think tank fellows serve 6-month renewable terms, with training, mentorship, and placement matching. For the 2027 cohort, base salaries are $78K/year (junior), $130K/year (fellow), and $190K+/year (senior), plus a $17K/year benefits-equivalent stipend, $3K professional development stipend, and up to $3K relocation support; applicants must be authorized to work in the US (no visa sponsorship, though first-year OPT is supported for think tank placements) and willing to live in the DC area.

structured.stipend: $78K–$190K+/year base salary plus $17K/year benefits-equivalent stipend, $3K professional development, up to $3K relocation
structured.duration: 1 year renewable up to 2 years (6-month renewable terms for junior think tank fellows)

name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed – applications for Spring 2027 closed September 27, 2026
current_details: The IAPS AI Policy Fellowship is a fully funded, 3-month program (Spring 2027 cohort) for professionals from varied backgrounds building practical AI governance skills, offered in Research and Applied tracks. Fellows receive $18K and Senior Fellows $24K stipends, with an extra $3K for those on the D.C. or London track, plus travel and accommodation support. All fellows attend a 2-week in-person kickoff in Washington, D.C. (February 22 – March 5, 2027), then continue in D.C., London, or remotely with an expert mentor.

name: Longitude DC Intensive
current_deadline: Closed - express interest for next cohort
current_details: A fully funded eight-day AI policy program in Washington, DC for people with a technical AI safety background who want to explore how their expertise could contribute to the policy ecosystem. 15 participants spend the program in talks, hands-on workshops, and networking with DC policy organizations, covering US government and AI policy foundations, career mapping, and post-program support (warm intros, advising). Participation is free with DC housing, meals on program days, and US travel covered; applicants need an undergraduate degree, AI safety context, and must be US citizens or currently based in the US.

structured.stipend: Fully funded (housing, meals, US travel covered)

name: RAND CAST Fellows
current_details: The RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) page now presents general ways to get involved rather than a dedicated fellowship application cycle: staff roles in the U.S. via RAND's jobs portal (currently Senior Research Lead – AI Security Portfolio and Research Lead – AI Cyber Testing & Evaluation), RAND Europe openings in the U.K., Belgium, and the Netherlands, and degree pathways through the RAND School of Public Policy. Graduate options include the 18-month M.Phil. and 3–5 year Pardee Ph.D. in Policy Analysis (both with on-the-job training on RAND projects), plus 9-month master's degrees in National Security Policy and Technology Policy. The center also invites open-ended collaboration inquiries through a contact form.

structured.location: U.S. (incl. Santa Monica, Washington DC) and Europe (U.K., Belgium, Netherlands)

name: Tarbell AI Journalism Fellowship
current_details: The Tarbell Fellowship is a one-year program for journalists and subject-matter experts covering artificial intelligence, combining a three-month remote AI and journalism fundamentals course, a weeklong in-person summit, and a nine-month newsroom placement at outlets such as CBS News, The Bureau of Investigative Journalism, MIT Technology Review, and TIME. Fellows earn $75,000–$120,000 depending on experience and location, while Senior Fellows (7+ years of journalism or AI experience) earn $115,000–$135,000. 2027-28 partner newsrooms are based in Hong Kong, London, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington D.C., so applicants generally need the right to work in the U.S., U.K., or Hong Kong.

structured.location: Hong Kong, London, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington D.C.
structured.program_dates: June 7 – Aug. 6, 2027 training; summit Aug. 16–20, 2027 (TBC); placement Sept. 2027 – May 2028

name: Andon Labs — Summer 2026 Role
current_details: Andon Labs is a Y Combinator W24 startup (founded 2023) building autonomous organizations without humans in the loop, based in San Francisco with a team of 11. The company is listed as Active, but no job openings are currently posted on the YC jobs platform.

name: ARC Visiting Researcher
current_deadline: Rolling — visiting researcher positions offered year-round
current_details: The Alignment Research Center (ARC) is hiring researchers, primarily for visiting researcher positions offered year-round, which typically run ~10 weeks with flexible duration. Most team members join as visiting researchers first so both sides can test fit; direct permanent hires face significantly higher requirements. Successful candidates usually have a strong theoretical background in math, physics, or computer science, with empirical ML experience a plus but not required. ARC is also tentatively accepting expressions of interest for automation engineers working on automating its research activities.

name: CHAI Internship (UC Berkeley)
current_details: A research internship at UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI) for people with a background in machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or related fields who want to move into human-compatible AI research. Interns work on a project supervised by (and usually proposed by) a CHAI mentor, typically producing first-author workshop papers, over 12–16 weeks with flexible start dates (internships usually begin around May). Compensation is $5,000/month in person at UC Berkeley and $3,500/month remote; international applicants are accepted.

name: CLR Summer Research Fellowship
current_details: The Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR) runs an annual two-month Summer Research Fellowship, usually at its London office, where fellows work on s-risk, AI safety and cooperative AI research questions under the supervision of a CLR researcher or external expert. Fellows typically receive a salary of £4,925/month if based in London, plus professional development and health/wellbeing budgets, with visa sponsorship available for international applicants. The program usually starts in June or July and has been CLR's main hiring pipeline — most researchers hired in the last four years were former fellows.

structured.program_dates: Usually begins June or July; takes place between June and September

name: Constellation Astra Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — applications closed Sep 26, 2026; expression of interest form open for the next cohort
current_details: Astra is Constellation's flagship 5-month, fully funded, in-person fellowship at its Berkeley research center, pairing emerging talent with senior mentors across an Empirical Research stream and a Strategy & Governance stream. Fellows receive a $8,400/month stipend, up to ~$15K/month in compute for empirical researchers, visa support, workspace, and dedicated research management and career support. Over 80% of the first cohort now work full-time in AI safety at organizations such as Redwood Research, METR, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, CAISI, and the UK AI Security Institute; prior AI safety experience is not required.

name: DeepMind Student Researcher
current_deadline: Rolling — see Google Careers for 2026-2027 cycle listings
current_details: Google DeepMind's Student Researcher Program is a paid, in-person internship placing students enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's or PhD programs alongside leading AI researchers at Google DeepMind, Google Research and other Google AI teams. Placements run 12–24 weeks with a commitment of five days per week at a Google office. A single application, organized by degree level (BS, MS, PhD) and location, is considered for all relevant roles across Google's AI teams.

structured.location: In-person at a Google office (location varies)

name: LASR Labs — Summer 2026
current_deadline: Not yet announced — express interest for the June–September 2027 cohort
current_details: LASR Labs is a 13-week technical AI safety research programme in London where participants work in teams of 3-4 with an experienced supervisor to take a project from proposal to publication. Participants receive a £15,000 stipend plus food, office space and travel, working full-time in person from the London Initiative for Safe AI alongside other AI safety organisations. Alumni have gone on to UK AISI, Apollo Research, OpenAI, Geodesic Research and Coefficient Giving, and LASR papers have appeared at NeurIPS, ICLR and ICML — including three NeurIPS 2025 main conference papers (one oral) and an ICML 2025 workshop best paper award.

name: OpenAI Emerging Talent
current_details: OpenAI's Emerging Talent hub gathers the company's early-career pathways — internships, a research residency, and full-time roles in research, applied engineering, and product for people with 0–3 years of experience. It's aimed at recent graduates and self-taught learners who want to help build safe, beneficial AI, with roles posted continuously on the OpenAI careers board. Prospective applicants can also join the Emerging Talent Community for networking, virtual Q&As, and community events, and consult the OpenAI Interview Guide and Charter.

name: Tilde Research
current_details: Tilde Research is a mechanistic interpretability lab (backed by Khosla Ventures) currently listing 3 open technical roles: ML Researcher, ML Engineer, and Kernel Engineer. Each role is offered as either an internship or full-time position and is based on-site in San Francisco. Postings have been live since July 2025 and are reviewed on a rolling basis through the Ashby job board.

name: Virtue AI
current_details: Virtue AI is an AI security and compliance platform founded by Bo Li and Dawn Song. The company offers positions across research, engineering, operations, marketing, and sales in San Francisco, but currently has no open positions listed on their job board.

name: Coefficient Giving — Project Tailwind
current_details: Project Tailwind is Coefficient Giving's call for founders to launch ambitious new AI safety organisations, funded across three tiers: pre-seed $200K–$2M, seed $2M–$20M, and scale $20M–$200M, typically covering 18–36 months of runway. Applicants can pitch their own idea or take on one of Coefficient's published unsolved problems in AI safety. Pre-seed applicants do not need an existing legal entity, and non-US teams and public-benefit for-profits are eligible.

name: Thinking Machines Lab — Safety Research Grants
current_details: Thinking Machines Lab is offering Tinker grants of up to $50,000 in API/compute credits for safety research on open-weight models, announced alongside their Inkling and Inkling-Small open-weight releases. Priority directions include making models safer to open (differential defense-vs-offense capability uplift, large-scale hazardous-data classifiers, tamper-resistant safety training), understanding alignment failure modes (emergent misalignment from narrow fine-tuning, reward hacking and chain-of-thought oversight gaming), and measuring and forecasting risk (worst-case and marginal risk estimation under adversarial fine-tuning). The list is explicitly non-exhaustive — any safety project that could be accelerated by additional Tinker credits is welcome.

structured.stipend: Up to $50K in Tinker API credits

name: IFP — The Launch Sequence RFP
current_details: IFP's Launch Sequence RFP was a rolling call for short (200–400 word) pitches for projects that accelerate science, strengthen security, or adapt institutions in anticipation of advanced AI. Authors of published proposals received a $10,000 honorarium, help turning the pitch into a concrete project plan, introductions to philanthropic funders, and headhunting support for a project lead, plus guidance from an advisory panel including Wojciech Zaremba, Tom Kalil, Matt Clifford, Kathleen Fisher, and George Church. $1,000 bounties were also offered for successful referrals and for new ideas that ended up published.

name: Paradigm 3 Research Fund
current_details: Paradigm 3's research fund supports external work on measuring and forecasting AI capabilities and impacts, alongside its in-house research. Current grantees are estimating the externalities of today's AI systems (starting with time lost to authentication challenges), decomposing benchmark gains into cheating, memorization, shallow generalization and OOD generalization, and studying when and how slowing AI progress would be desirable. They invite proposals on centaur evals, 'guardian angel' user-aligned models, the virtue-vs-rules alignment divide, generalization gaps, scaling and 'unhobbling', automated science, compute growth, job displacement, specialized vs. generalist AI, and recursive self-improvement — prospective grantees email hi@paradigm3.org.

name: grantmaking.ai Launch Round
current_details: grantmaking.ai's inaugural Launch Round offered $1M total for work reducing x-risk from AI, with grants of $5k–$50k per applicant. A single short application created a public project page and funding ask visible to every funder on the platform, reviewed by grantmakers including Gavin Leech (Arb Research), Ryan Kidd (MATS), and Marcus Abramovitch (AltX). The round ran from June 29, 2025, with guaranteed review for applications by July 13 and decisions by July 31; applications are now closed, though projects can still be listed with a public funding ask that stays up after the round ends.

structured.program_dates: Applications opened June 29, 2025; decisions by July 31, 2025

name: Falcon Fund (Manifund)
current_details: The Falcon Fund is a Manifund-hosted animal welfare fund led by regrantor Marcus Abramovitch, making rapid (under 1 week) early-stage grants of $25K–$150K, with a particular focus on the intersection of animal welfare and transformative AI. Priority areas include animal harm benchmarks, animal welfare constitutions for frontier models, watchdog work on AI in factory farming, and raising animal welfare salience inside AI labs. Launched April 2026, it has raised $380,132 from 18 donors toward a $2M goal, with all grants and rationales published publicly; grantmaking is largely active/outbound, though contact is open via marcus.s.abramovitch@gmail.com.

structured.duration: Decisions in under 1 week; funds wired within ~3 days
structured.program_dates: Launched Apr 24, 2026; initial $2M raise targeted by May 15, 2026

name: MARS — Cambridge AI Safety Hub
current_deadline: Closed May 10, 2026 — check for next cycle
current_details: MARS is a part-time, hybrid AI safety research programme from the Cambridge AI Safety Hub that pairs teams of 2–4 mentees with experienced mentors to produce publishable technical and governance research. The structure includes 2–4 weeks of prework, a 1-week in-person kick-off in Cambridge (Jul 13–19 or Jul 20–26), and 8–10 weeks of remote part-time work at 8–15+ hours/week. It is unpaid but free to attend, with travel, accommodation, meals, a $2k+ compute budget, Claude Max (5x), and a dedicated research manager provided.

structured.duration: ~12-15 weeks (2-4 weeks prework, 1-week in-person kick-off, 8-10 weeks remote)

name: TARA — Technical Alignment Research Accelerator
current_deadline: Closed — Round 1 2027 applications not yet open
current_details: TARA (Technical Alignment Research Accelerator) is a free 14-week part-time technical AI safety program for talent across the Asia-Pacific region, built on the ARENA curriculum. Participants attend full-day Saturday in-person sessions (~7.5 hours) plus 2-7 hours of weekly independent study covering transformer architectures, mechanistic interpretability, RL and model evaluations, culminating in a 3-week research project. Round 2 2026 runs 5 September – 12 December across 10 cities with ~194 participants; a refundable commitment bond applies (e.g. $200 AUD, ₹3,000 INR, ¥12,000 JPY).
