name: AI Safety Camp
current_details: AI Safety Camp is an online, part-time AI safety research program (12th edition) where participants join one of 32 preselected projects spanning stop/pause AI, policy and governance, agentic risk and oversight, evaluations, mech-interp, and AI safety education. Team members are expected to commit 10 hours/week and attend weekly meetings across the ~3.5-month program, which runs January to April 2027 and ends with an online final-presentations conference. Applicants can apply to specific projects or submit one generic application covering all of them.

structured.program_dates: Jan 9 – Apr 26, 2027 (opening weekend Jan 9–10; projects Jan 12 – Apr 23; final presentations Apr 24–26)

name: Dovetail Research Fellowship
current_details: Dovetail is a research group pursuing foundational mathematics research aimed at understanding the nature of AI agents, with the mission of helping humanity safely navigate the creation of powerful AI systems. It is funded in part by the Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF) and the Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA), and publishes its research agenda as a public wiki. The landing page links to a Jobs section but lists no fellowship cohort dates, stipend, location, or application details.

name: Generator Residency
current_details: Generator is a 3-month residency in Berkeley run by Kairos and Constellation for AI safety generalists — agentic executors from operations, communications, policy, engineering, CS and other backgrounds — who pitch, build, and ship projects that strengthen the AI safety ecosystem. Residents receive a $8,500/month stipend, mentorship from advisors across the field, and support landing full-time AI safety roles; the Winter 2027 cohort runs January 18 – April 9, 2027. The first cohort (summer 2026) had 27 residents and produced projects like Longitude, Talent Commons and Lateral.

name: AIXI Labs Fellowship
current_details: Universal Algorithmic Intelligence (uaiasi.com) is a community hub for researchers working on Solomonoff induction, AIXI, and the mathematical foundations of intelligence, using computability theory and probability to work backward from idealized reasoning toward practical algorithms. The site hosts regular online research and paper-discussion meetings plus an "Introduction to Universal Artificial Intelligence" reading group as an on-ramp for new students and researchers from other fields, and it periodically awards fellowships for UAI/AI-safety research. Recent activity is community blog content — talks and study-group notes on MDL, meta-learning, and Solomonoff induction — with no active fellowship call currently posted.

name: Frame Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — Cohort 2.0 applications closed August 5, 2026; express interest for the next cycle
current_details: The Frame Fellowship is a 10-week accelerator in San Francisco for content creators making high-quality video that educates the public about AI and its societal and economic implications. Fellows receive housing, meals, and a $10,000 stipend, plus mentorship from creators like Rob Miles, Drew Spartz, Liron Shapira, Chana Messinger, and Petr Lebedev, across two tracks (Independent and Amplifier, the latter embedding with orgs such as MATS, Apart Research, Andon Labs, the AI Digest, Humans in Control, The Midas Project, and CAIS). Cohort 2.0 ran September 7 – November 15, 2026; applications are closed and an expression-of-interest form collects sign-ups for the next cycle.

name: Collective Intelligence Project Research Fellowship
current_details: The Collective Intelligence Project's pilot Research Fellowship supports 3 fellows for 6 months to conduct original research with CIP's proprietary datasets — Global Dialogues multi-country AI attitude surveys across 70+ countries (7+ rounds), Collective Generation deliberation data, and the Weval evaluation platform (100+ blueprints, 112+ model configurations). It is remote and non-residential at 5–10 hours/week with bi-weekly virtual lab meetings and a fixed $9,000 stipend paid across three milestone-based tranches (onboarding, analysis, final draft). Aimed primarily at late-stage PhD candidates (ABD) and early-career postdocs in political science, computational social science, sociology, or CS/ML, though independent and international scholars are welcome.

name: Frontier AI Security Residency
current_details: The Frontier AI Security Residency (FASR) is an 8-week, fully funded in-person research and engineering programme in Cambridge, UK, run by ERA with Heron and the Oxford Hardware AI Governance Lab. Residents work alongside mentors from leading AI hardware and cybersecurity teams on concrete projects in hardware-enabled verification, cybersecurity and policy, with talks, poster sessions at ERA conferences, and a live-in cohort community. The inaugural cohort runs 12 Oct – 4 Dec 2026 and is currently underway; the site offers only a mailing list for future updates, with no live application form.

name: Heron AI Security Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - express interest in future cohorts
current_details: Heron's AI Security Research Fellowship pairs experienced cybersecurity professionals (5+ years) with AI security field leaders across 10-12 research teams, each made up of an expert advisor, 2-4 cyber professionals, a project manager and a technical advisor. Focus areas span AI infrastructure and hardware security, technical AI governance, adversarial/model security, AI control and containment, and cybersecurity evaluations. The autumn cycle ran 3 months (September–November 2026), remote-first with coworking hubs in London, Tel Aviv and San Francisco, at 8-30 hours/week; it is unpaid but teams receive $1,000+ in compute, Claude Code Team accounts and up to $5K per team in conference travel support, with a guaranteed presentation at the AI Security Forum in Tel Aviv.

structured.stipend: Unpaid ($1,000+ compute credits, up to $5K/team travel support)
structured.location: Remote-first; coworking hubs in London, Tel Aviv, San Francisco

name: CBAI AIxBiosecurity Fellowship
current_deadline: Fall 2026 cohort closed (ran Oct 13 – Dec 18, 2026); summer 2027 applications open early 2027 — EOI form open now
current_details: The CBAI AIxBiosecurity Research Fellowship is a fully-funded 10-week research program in Harvard Square, Cambridge, MA focused on AI-enabled biological risk — dangerous capability evaluations, safeguards and unlearning for bio-relevant models, threat modeling, biosurveillance, DNA synthesis screening, and governance of compute, model access and dual-use publication. Fellows receive a $15,000 stipend, housing for relocators, free weekday meals, 24/7 office access, weekly 1:1 mentorship from researchers at SecureBio, RAND, Harvard, Active Site, Protectome and LatchBio, plus ~$1,500/week in compute credits and possible extension funding up to 6 months. It runs alongside the CBAI AI Safety Research Fellowship for a combined cohort of 40 fellows; students, postdocs, recent grads and experienced professionals (as Senior Fellows) are welcome, and J-1 visa sponsorship will be available for the summer cycle.

structured.program_dates: Oct 13 – Dec 18, 2026 (fall 2026 cohort); next cohort summer 2027

name: AI Security Bootcamp — London
current_deadline: TBD — applications currently open for the Feb 2027 London cohort
current_details: AI Security Bootcamp London is a 7-day intensive, fully funded programme for experienced security professionals working to secure frontier AI systems, running Feb 7–13, 2027 in London. The curriculum spans threat modelling, adversarial attacks, LLM and infrastructure security, weight security and formal methods, data centre security, AI control, and hardware governance, delivered via lectures, demos, guest speakers, and hands-on red/blue team exercises. Tuition, meals, materials, and London accommodation are covered with need-based travel support; 20 participants are accepted and 7+ years of hands-on security experience is required (no prior AI/ML background needed, pre-work provided).

structured.stipend: Fully funded (tuition, meals, materials, accommodation; need-based travel support)

name: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST)
current_details: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) is an in-person, fully funded training programme developed by SASH, a technical AI governance research organisation working across East and West. It now runs two pathways: a technical track for security and ML practitioners with hands-on labs on frontier models, agents and the surrounding systems, and a policy track giving policymakers technical AI security literacy they can translate into policy for their jurisdiction. Cohorts are hosted in a single location each but draw participants globally, with curriculum, 'after FAST' support and FAQ detail on the site.

name: FAS AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship
GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program
current_details: The GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program is a bipartisan, part-time, 12-week program for U.S. policy professionals in government and think tanks, building a technically-informed understanding of the AI policy landscape. It requires about 5 hours per week (3 hours of independent reading plus 2 hours of evening synchronous sessions, attended in person at GovAI's D.C. office near DuPont Circle or remotely) and is free of charge, with dinner provided for in-person attendees. Eligible applicants include executive and legislative branch staff, fellows, interns, detailees, military and national lab personnel, and think tank researchers, with preference for the D.C. metro area; completion requires attending 9 of 12 sessions, writing a policy memo or op-ed, and passing an interview-based exam.

structured.location: Washington, D.C. (GovAI office near DuPont Circle) or remote
structured.program_dates: Early September – early December 2026 (break for Thanksgiving week)

name: Vista Institute for AI Policy
current_details: The Vista Institute for AI Policy (a fiscally sponsored project of Rethink Priorities) builds the academic field of AI law and policy through part-time virtual courses, DC workshops, and a fellowship. Its 2026 virtual courses — National Security Law and AI (Aug 10–26), AI Agents and the Law Module 1 (Aug 19–Sep 4) and Module 2 (Sep 7–Oct 2) — have all concluded, as have its July 2026 Washington, DC workshops. The AI Law and Policy Fellowship sponsors students and recent graduates for independent research with mentor guidance or research-assistant placements, but has no public application: completing a Vista course is what makes you eligible to apply.

name: Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH)
current_details: The Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH) is a Singapore-based organisation bridging governments, academia and industry across East and West on trustworthy frontier AI, with applied technical governance research spanning verification mechanisms, frontier safety evaluations and agent governance. It runs the Singapore AI Safety Fellowship for researchers and the Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) program for policymakers and practitioners, alongside public talks, private convenings and a co-working space in central Singapore. The homepage advertises open roles and states SASH is hiring globally, but lists no specific application windows or dates.

name: Center for Technology & Statecraft
current_details: The Center for Technology & Statecraft (CTS) is a non-partisan AI policy research initiative based in Washington, DC, founded by former White House NSC and Commerce official Saif M. Khan. Its team of technologists, analysts, and former policymakers — including alumni of RAND, GovAI, CNAS, Epoch AI, and CSET — produces technical, forward-looking research on the AI transition, US-China competition, semiconductor supply chains, export controls, and compute infrastructure. The site links to a Careers page but the homepage lists no specific internship, fellowship, application window, or deadline.

structured.location: Washington, DC (1225 Union St NE, Ste 800)

name: Secure AI Project
current_details: Secure AI Project is a San Francisco-based AI policy and safety advocacy nonprofit that develops and advocates for pragmatic policies to reduce risks of severe harm from advanced AI, including work on California legislation and bills it supports. The homepage links to About, Contact, Donate, Bills We Support, Policies, and Careers pages but lists no specific internship, fellowship, or job openings, application windows, or deadlines. Interested applicants should monitor the Careers page for postings.

name: SAIGE Incubator — Safe AI Germany
current_deadline: Next cohort to be announced — register your interest
current_details: The SAIGE Incubator is Safe AI Germany's part-time, remote research fellowship pairing newcomers with expert mentors in small teams across four tracks: Technical AI Safety, Technical AI Governance, AI Governance & Policy, and Communication & Fieldbuilding. It runs 3 months with an optional extension at 5–20 hours per week; the first cohort (Spring 2026) drew 226 applications and supported 73 mentees on 22 projects, several of which became NeurIPS 2026 workshop papers. 74% of surveyed mentees said they would not have worked on AI safety without SAIGE.

structured.program_dates: Spring 2026 cohort: 27 Apr – 31 Jul 2026; next cohort TBA

name: BlueDot Impact — Incubator Week
current_deadline: Not yet announced — express interest anytime
current_details: BlueDot Impact's Incubator Week is a 5-day, all-expenses-paid founder sprint in San Francisco where you and a friend, colleague, or prospective co-founder test-drive founding an AI safety organization — covering founding 101, threat modelling, building and pressure-testing interventions, and a final pitch worth up to $200k in seed grant funding (delivered within two weeks). It's aimed at people working in or adjacent to AI safety, biosecurity, cyber, or other catastrophic-risk fields who are ready to leave their current role if the week goes well; no polished idea is required and solo applicants are considered in exceptional cases. Past cohorts total 50 participants who have raised $10M+ externally, and referrals earn $2,000 per accepted person.

structured.stipend: Up to $200k in grant funding; all expenses paid

name: Neolithic
current_details: Neolithic is an engineering-first nonprofit startup in San Francisco (founded 2026, fiscally sponsored by BERI and funded by Coefficient Giving and Foresight Institute) building open-source, agentic tools and infrastructure for defensive AI safety research — including RIDArena (rogue internal deployment control settings, built with Redwood Research), agent swarm infrastructure, a mock AGI lab, and critical-infrastructure cyber ranges. It is hiring a Member of Technical Staff (full-time, in-person San Francisco, $180K+ plus benefits and US visa sponsorship) as one of its first hires, with end-to-end project ownership and direct collaboration with leading safety organisations. It also invites AI labs, safety orgs and independent researchers to request custom tooling, which Neolithic will build and maintain for free.

name: d_model
current_details: d_model is a fundamental AI research lab partnering with frontier labs to turn their models into capable interpretability and alignment researchers, building RL environments for open-ended interpretability tasks that teach agents to do real research rather than reward-hack. Alongside partnerships, the lab pursues independent interpretability research, with publications on LLM-agent-discovered concept-editing algorithms (July 2026), how models represent program nullability, and steering characters via interpretability. Career interest is collected through a general Hiring Interest Form rather than a formal application window; the team page already lists a cohort of summer 2027 interns.

name: Allelo
current_deadline: Closed — Pivotal application deadline was 1 November 2026
current_details: Allelo is a new AI safety research initiative (fiscally sponsored by Rethink Priorities) studying what propensities and character traits make AI agents safe to deploy in complex, multi-agent, sometimes adversarial real-world settings, with an initial focus on susceptibility to influence. It aims to produce concrete agent-design recommendations for frontier labs, regulators, and certification bodies. The current get-involved route is a mentored project with founder Cecilia Elena Tilli in the Q1 2027 Pivotal AI Safety Fellowship — 15 weeks full-time and in person in London (18 January – 30 April 2027), with applications handled entirely by Pivotal.

name: RESI — Institute for Responsible Superintelligence
current_deadline: Interest form open for inaugural workshop — December 4, 2026
current_details: RESI (Institute for Responsible Superintelligence) is an independent nonprofit AI safety research institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts building the scientific foundations for superintelligence that is "safe by design" — safety properties specified in advance and achieved by mechanisms whose guarantees can be analyzed before deployment, borrowing the modern cryptography playbook of definitions, constructions, and provable guarantees. Founded by Turing Award winner Shafi Goldwasser, Gödel Prize winner Vinod Vaikuntanathan, and former OpenAI researcher Adam Tauman Kalai, its work spans verification and oversight, control and delegation, composition, and multi-agent dynamics, supported by grants from Coefficient Giving, Schmidt Sciences, and AISTOF. RESI is hosting its inaugural Safe-by-Design Superintelligence workshop in Cambridge, MA with speakers including Boaz Barak, Zico Kolter, Vincent Conitzer, and Adam Gleave, and runs a reading group, seminars, and open roles via its "Join us" page.

name: Verified Mechanisms
current_details: Verified Mechanisms is an independent, grant-funded (via Manifund) research project building a formally verified autoresearch pipeline for theoretical mechanistic interpretability, where multiple frontier LLM agents collaborate to generate theorems that are machine-checked in Lean 4. The pilot question asks how many attention heads are required to compute a Boolean function, with outputs including an open-source multi-agent orchestration harness, the xorformer theorem ledger repo, and an oral paper at the AutoMLR Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. There is no formal application form — the team of research leads, interpretability researchers, engineers and Talmenta mentees invites interested people to join the Discord or email hello@verifiedmechanisms.ai.

name: PauseAI — Vacancies
current_details: PauseAI's vacancies page currently lists no open positions, but the organisation welcomes spontaneous applications from people passionate about its mission to pause frontier AI development. Candidates can email a CV and a brief cover letter to vacancies@pauseai.info; applications are kept on file and reviewed when paid roles next open, though a response is not guaranteed.

name: ML4Good Technical Bootcamp
current_deadline: Not yet announced — join notification list
current_details: ML4Good's Technical Programme is a free, residential AI safety bootcamp covering transformers built from scratch, LLM agents, interpretability, RLHF, evaluations, technical governance, and a 2-day capstone project with mentorship and 1-on-1 career sessions. Food, accommodation and teaching are provided at no cost, travel may be reimbursed, and cohorts are organised regionally so participants come from the same area; all sessions run in English. It targets people with some coding experience (coding is ~25-30% of the curriculum) who are committed to contributing substantially to AI safety — alumni have gone on to MATS, SaferAI, UK AISI and the EU AI Office, and 98% of participants recommend it.

structured.stipend: Free (food, accommodation, teaching covered; travel may be reimbursed)
structured.location: Regional cohorts worldwide — past venues include Hong Kong, France, UK, Canada, Germany, South Africa, Singapore, Brazil, Italy, Colombia, Switzerland

name: Successif
current_details: Successif offers free, expert-guided career development for experienced professionals transitioning into AI risk reduction work. Support includes a dedicated 1:1 advisor, resume and application feedback, mock interviews, expert-led workshops and self-paced courses on technical, policy and media topics, direct introductions to AI risk organizations with early access to jobs, and a peer community via Discord and social events. Specialized tracks include an AI Policy Strategy Fellowship and a Women's Program for women and other underrepresented groups.

name: MIT AI Risk Initiative
current_details: The MIT AI Risk Initiative (at MIT FutureTech) is an ongoing research project producing open, CC BY 4.0-licensed data and frameworks for identifying, prioritizing, and managing AI risks. Its tools include the AI Risk Repository (1,700+ risks from 65 frameworks), an AI Incident Tracker, a global governance database mapping AI laws and policies to risk domains, a mitigations database (2,206 mitigations from 47 frameworks), company disclosure data covering the world's 200 largest firms, an expert survey of 272 international AI experts, a new existential-risk scenario review, and the AI Risk Navigator that connects all datasets via shared taxonomies. There are no applications — the site offers a newsletter, a blog with research updates, and a "get in touch" route for partnerships.

name: ALIGN — AI Alignment Network
current_details: ALIGN (AI Alignment Network), a Japanese non-profit general incorporated association founded in September 2023, is recruiting volunteer staff for event operations, community management, PR/social media, research and writing, website maintenance, and organizational administration. Applicants should ideally commit 3–4+ hours per week, hold basic admin/IT skills, and share ALIGN's values (dialogue and trust, inclusivity, agility, effectiveness, hope); English communication ability is welcomed, and depending on fit and ALIGN's finances a paid role of roughly 1–2 days per week may be discussed. Apply via the Contact form with name, affiliation, SNS accounts, experience (100–400 characters), what you'd like to do at ALIGN (~400 characters), and availability, followed by document screening and an online interview.

structured.stipend: Volunteer (possible paid role of ~1–2 days/week depending on fit and finances)

name: Vegas AI Security Forum
current_deadline: TLV '26 on Nov 22, 2026 — applications open (DC Reading Group rolling)
current_details: The AI Security Forum is an invite-based event series convening experts in AI, cybersecurity, and national security to secure powerful AI models, with editions in Las Vegas (during Black Hat/DEF CON week), DC, Tel Aviv, and Paris. The most recent Vegas AI Security Forum '26 took place Aug 6, 2026 and has concluded; applications are currently open for TLV '26 in Israel and a rolling US-based DC Reading Group. The forum is fiscally sponsored by Hack Club, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

structured.location: Las Vegas, Washington DC, Tel Aviv, Paris

name: ELLIS Institute Tübingen — AI Safety & Alignment Group
current_details: The AI Safety and Alignment Group at the ELLIS Institute Tübingen, led by Maksym Andriushchenko (EPFL postdoctoral researcher and ELLIS Member), develops technical solutions to reduce risks from general-purpose AI models. Research covers alignment of autonomous LLM agents, rigorous AI evaluations, public communication about frontier model capabilities and risks, and how models generalize from training data. The group lists four PhD students, one current intern and three intern alumni in Tübingen, Germany; this is a group overview page with no application window — check the institute's Careers page for open PhD and internship positions.
